# Many local bricks, one binary field

[Each process owns a piece of the field. The file describes the global array.]{.lesson-deck}
:::

The old `write_results` demonstration assigned four hard-coded values to
each of exactly two ranks. Here the decomposition supplies every rank's
brick, so the same program works on one or multiple processes. An affine
field makes the expected file values unambiguous:

$$
u(x,y,z)=1+x+2y+3z.
$$ {#eq-field}

The default grid has size $8\times4\times2$, origin $(-1,2,3)$ and
spacing $(.25,.5,.75)$. Nonzero geometry catches a common mistake:
writing local array indices as though they were physical coordinates.

## Tell MPI-IO where the local brick belongs

```{.cpp include="model.cpp" snippet="binary" dedent=4}
```

All processes in the communicator call `write` and `read`. The global
dimensions, local dimensions and global offsets define the MPI file
view. The owned buffer is compact, so its length is exactly the local
brick product. Ghost padding is not part of this raw file.

The filename's increment is 5, hence `results/field_0005.bin`. Writing
a file does not store the field's geometry or a complete simulation
checkpoint. Keep that metadata separately, or use
[the snapshot series](../vtk-series/index.qmd) or
[checkpoint service](../checkpoint-restart/index.qmd) as appropriate.

## Inspect the global layout independently

The example additionally reads the complete file on rank zero using an
ordinary C++ binary stream:

```{.cpp include="model.cpp" snippet="read" dedent=6}
```

The flat offset is $i+N_x(j+N_yk)$: x varies fastest. This independent
read checks both values and ordering. The file contains exactly
$N_xN_yN_z$ native `double` values. It has no header, endianness tag or
geometry block; do not infer cross-platform portability from exact
round trips on the same platform.

## Run on a different partition

```sh
openpfc run model.cpp input.json --source-root .. --launcher=none
openpfc run model.cpp input.json --source-root .. --ranks=2 --launcher=mpirun
```

Both runs should print that all values were restored exactly. The tests
also decode the raw file independently in Python and compare every global
sample with @eq-field. Change `n` and predict the file size before running.
The writer and reader are destroyed before the MPI environment is finalized.

Keep the [model](model.cpp), [input](input.json) and
[geometry helper](../lesson.hpp) together.
:::
